newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo says Europe's healthcare outlook "complex".
newsitem.headline: Glaxo says Europe's healthcare outlook "complex".

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Monday that the medium-term outlook for the healthcare industry in Europe was likely to become "more complex" as European Union members strove to meet criteria for monetary union.

In a speech to the FT World Pharmaceuticals Conference, Glaxo Wellcome chief operating officer Sean Lance said the demands of monetary union had prompted a "wholesale renegotiation of the social contract."
"As healthcare represents as much as 15 percent of public expenditure in some countries, it will not be immune from government attempts to meet the Maastricht criteria."
Lance said he believed lessons had been earned from the "short-termism" seen in the early 1990s "as government sought to make quick savings."

And he added: "Europe will remain a highly attractive market, but as the ratchet of budgetary pressure turns again it will be the companies who cannot demonstrate the clinical and economic benefits of their products who will feel the pinch."
Lance, who is Glaxo Wellcome's chief excutive-designate, also told the conference that pharmaceuticals had been, "the signal failure of the (European) single market."
He said there had been no linkage in Europe between the free movement of pharmaceutical products and freedom for companies to price products as they wished.
"The ambivalence of governments and the Commission in this regard must be resolved if Europe is to progress as a base for the industry."
Lance said Europe also lacked a "coherent basis for the protection of biotechnology inventions."

But he added that "the single biggest challenge" faced by the drugs industry worldwide was "to win global acceptance for robust intellectual property protection...we have not succeeded in getting the basic philosophy of intellectual property across to enough governments."
